A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reward Auditor work. The main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; the shorter v2 reflects layout changes rather than missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original audits of 26 reward models, downstream alignment experiments in Section 5, and supplementary empirical analyses in Appendices B and E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original reward-model audits, downstream alignment results and supplementary empirical analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 retain the same confidence differences, paired permutation test, count-based p-value, effect-size reporting and group-aware Benjamini–Hochberg procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five RM Bench subsets, Reward Bench chat subset, Reward Bench2 math and safety subsets, ten perturbations and downstream dialogue alignment task.

E2.justification: Appendix B retains the same comparisons involving the paired t-test, Wilcoxon signed-rank test and accuracy-change evaluation. The audited model sets are unchanged; the newly cited works are not added as experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A retain the same model selection, clean versus perturbed training design, PPO settings and 100-prompt GPT-4o evaluation. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the normality checks, test-statistic and distribution robustness comparisons, benchmark meta-evaluation, perturbation correlations and clustering, and accuracy-versus-suitability analyses unchanged.

E5.justification: Significance thresholds, statistical testing procedures, significance markers and confidence-band reporting remain unchanged. No repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-estimation information is added.

E6.justification: Numerical tables and figures are unchanged, but Section 5.1.3 corrects the reported trend from subjective-domain robustness to objective-domain robustness, consistent with Figure 2. Section 5.1.2 replaces '80.7% ... across all perturbations' with '21 out of 26 ... both controlled and stylized'; this revised scope is not clearly supported by Table 1, which marks significance in both groups for only 15 models.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and Appendix C lemmas, theorems and proofs are unchanged. Replacing the prose symbol Δ with ΔM in Section 4.1.1 repairs notation without changing mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: suitability auditing, the perturbation suite, multiplicity control and downstream alignment relevance. Minor wording changes do not alter their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Explanations involving subjective evaluation, superficial cues, model specificity and downstream transfer remain unchanged, as do Appendix C.3's qualifications. v1 already contained the correct subjective-domain interpretation beneath its erroneous result headline.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same scoring details, prompts, hyperparameters and eight-A800 hardware disclosure. Code-access information is unchanged; the abstract URL is merely wrapped differently.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the references add Ding et al. (2025) on RoleRMBench/RoleRM and Wang et al. (2025) on multidimensional preference representations. This modestly broadens related-work coverage without redefining the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited wording, terminology and notation edits, an expanded affiliation, and replacement of the work-in-progress footer with 'Preprint'. The section structure is retained. Appendix C introduces a broken 'Appendix ??' reference where v1 correctly referenced C.2.

P2.justification: v2 removes excessive paragraph spacing on page 32 and repacks the existing Appendix E tables, placing Tables 6 and 7 together on page 34. Several captions receive small wording edits; figures and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Section 5.1.3's reversed headline resolves a misleading contradiction with Figure 2 and the existing discussion. Added related-work coverage and improved appendix spacing provide smaller benefits. These limited gains are partly offset by the new broken appendix reference and the unresolved support for the revised Table 1 summary.
